text:
The response provides a clear, well-structured overview that directly addresses both parts of the prompt. The listed components (collectors, storage, pump, controller) and considerations (location, climate, sizing, orientation, backup) are accurate and relevant for a residential solar thermal system. The five-step workflow follows a logical engineering sequence from demand assessment to commissioning.

However, the answer remains at a high level and omits several critical details expected in an actual design task: it does not distinguish between active/passive or direct/indirect system types, lacks mention of essential safety components (pressure relief valves, expansion tanks), freeze protection strategies (drainback or glycol loops), structural roof load calculations, pipe insulation, or specific sizing methodologies (e.g., collector area per gallon of demand). The workflow steps are also somewhat generic (e.g., "determine demand" without specifying load calculation methods). While accurate and helpful as an introductory framework, it lacks the technical depth required for a complete residential design specification.

Rating: [[7]]
